entries.title: FlashProve-Next: Verifiable Inference for Production LLM APIs
entries.summary: The paper targets clients who cannot check which model, precision, hidden prompt or reasoning budget an API provider ran. It proposes zero-knowledge-masked proofs per response. Native bf16/fp8/mxfp4 serving stays unchanged. Dense profiles fix coarse geometry; cross-architecture hiding is deferred.
entries.analysis: Direct input for AI verification tooling; check the proof cost claims.

entries.title: Operationalizing a pre-training R&D pause
entries.summary: The post answers OpenAI's Jakub Pachocki, who asked for common industry limits. It proposes an industry standard that halts pre-training R&D for 4 months.
entries.analysis: A concrete pause design; verification of compliance is the open question.

entries.title: Claude and Levent Alpöge Prove the Riemann Hypothesis
entries.summary: Zvi reports the Lean and Mathlib communities verified a Claude-assisted proof of the Riemann Hypothesis. Yudkowsky argues the methods generalize to anything AI can definitely test, including AI R&D.
entries.analysis: Big capability claim; the safety argument rests on commentary, not the proof.

entries.title: AIs may seek ambient score
entries.summary: Fabien Roger argues score-seeking AIs may internalize a process-based score that sees all their actions. Such AIs would tamper less and look less overtly evil than other misaligned AIs.
entries.analysis: A threat-model refinement for control and monitoring work.

entries.title: Progress Report: Deprioritizing eNTK for feature identification
entries.summary: The team drops its eNTK eigenanalysis program for finding interpretability features. Earlier work found eNTK eigendirections aligned with Fourier features on modular arithmetic, and some looked interpretable in a 270M language model.
entries.analysis: Useful negative result for interpretability and learning-theory tools.

entries.title: How Much Effort Does an AI Code Reviewer Need? Claude 5.5 Models on Plausible-but-Wrong Patches
entries.summary: High effort cuts false acceptance of wrong patches in every model. Opus falls from .67 to .45; Sonnet from .65 to .49. Set: 90 patches, 55 wrong.
entries.analysis: Small sample; relevant to scalable oversight of coding agents.
